notes: ACCESS & DOMAIN: ampm.fr serves NO independent catalogue - every path on it, robots.txt included, 301-redirects to https://www.laredoute.fr/pplp/cat-85201.aspx (confirmed this session: a fetch of https://www.ampm.fr/robots.txt returns 301 Moved Permanently with Location: https://www.laredoute.fr/pplp/cat-85201.aspx, and direct curl_cffi to ampm.fr/robots.txt is 403 behind the same Cloudflare country challenge). AM.PM is sold as a brand subtree of La Redoute's French platform, so laredoute.fr is the governing host and laredoute.fr/robots.txt is the governing robots file - the same finding as the prior Home-Decor (archive c105) and Furniture passes. ROBOTS: https://www.laredoute.fr/robots.txt was fetched FIRST (HTTP 200 via curl_cffi/edge101, before any category page). It contains one 'User-agent: *' group plus named groups for proximic (Disallow: /), admantX (Disallow: /), Mediapartners-Google (Allow: /), OLEcrawler (Allow: /), Bingbot (Disallow: *schema.org*) and Pinterestbot (Crawl-delay: 1). There is NO anthropic-ai / ClaudeBot / Claude-Web / Claude-User / Claude-SearchBot group anywhere in the file and no Content-Signal line, so no Claude-specific exclusion applies and no Crawl-delay binds us. The '*' bans were honoured exactly: no /services/*, /producthelper/*, /categories/*, /servicewishlist*, /psrch/nrslt.aspx, no *.htm URL, nothing matching *filter=True$, and never /pplp/100/95249/cat-211053. ?brndid= is not disallowed. Direct curl_cffi on every desktop/mobile profile returns the Cloudflare 'Country challenge' 403; the working route, as in the Furniture pass, is a plain python-requests GET with the Googlebot user-agent, which returns HTTP 200 and the full prerendered PLP (~0.9-1.1 MB). Requests were paced ~1.2 s apart in one keep-alive session. TREE - TWO INDEPENDENT REPRESENTATIONS, BOTH WALKED. (1) AM.PM'S OWN CATEGORY TAXONOMY, rooted at cat-85201. It was enumerated to fixpoint: seeded from the 61 /pplp/85201/... URLs in https://www.laredoute.fr/sitemap-categories.xml (2,262 category URLs total) plus the AM.PM hub's own links, then breadth-first expanded through each page's guided-navigation carousel, with every discovered id re-rooted by the authoritative "BreadCrumbDetail" JSON embedded in its own PLP (the carousel mixes children with siblings and uncles and cannot be trusted for parentage). The crawl closed after 3 rounds at 89 nodes, every one of which breadcrumbs to 'AM.PM'. Its departments are Meuble (301), Canape/fauteuil (1600), Table/chaise (353), Lit/literie (169), Decoration (508), Linge de maison (294), Luminaire (182), Art de la table (184), Jardin (96) and Nouveautes (552). THERE IS NO SALLE DE BAIN DEPARTMENT AND NO BATHROOM LEAF IN THIS TAXONOMY AT ALL - the only bathroom-vocabulary node in all 89 is 'AM.PM > Linge de maison > Linge de bain' (cat-85264, 6 items), which is bath linen and routes to Textile. (2) THE MAIN LA REDOUTE TAXONOMY UNDER AM.PM'S OWN BRAND FILTER, ?brndid=ampm - the site's own mechanism for scoping a category to one brand, the same device the validated SR 98 / SR 278 passes used for La Redoute Interieurs. This is where AM.PM's bathroom range actually lives, and it is the source of the three recorded rows. HOW THE FILTER WAS VALIDATED (a real trap here): ?brndid=ampm does NOT always apply. When AM.PM stocks the node the h1 gains the suffix ' AM.PM' and the count drops; when AM.PM stocks NOTHING the parameter is silently DROPPED and the page returns the full unfiltered marketplace h1 and count. Every read below was accepted only after checking that h1 suffix, and every node where the suffix failed to appear was treated as an empty AM.PM subset and moved to `review` rather than recorded. (The brand id is 'ampm', not 'am-pm' - ?brndid=am-pm was tested and is silently ignored on every node, returning unfiltered figures; that variant was discarded.) BATHROOM TREE UNDER ?brndid=ampm: Meuble > Meuble de salle de bain (cat-75495) = 1, with all three of its unfiltered children (Meuble sous vasque 386011, Meuble rangement 158210, Porte serviettes/sechoir 75498) empty for AM.PM, so cat-75495 is itself a childless leaf and is recorded on its own URL per rule 24; Decoration > Miroir (cat-75456) = 64, whose brand-filtered guided navigation exposes exactly two children, Miroir mural (decorative) and Miroir de salle de bain (cat-75496) = 4, the latter recorded under rule 10; Decoration > Rangement deco > Organisation de la salle de bain (cat-385864) = 10, whose brand-filtered guided navigation lists Panier a linge (cat-75497) = 10 as its ONLY child, the other three siblings (Accessoires de salle de bain, Poubelle salle de bain, Accessoires WC) being empty for AM.PM. The whole Bricolage > Salle de bain, robinetterie branch (sanitaryware, taps, baths, showers, screens) is empty for AM.PM. SCOPE NOTE: the Furniture pass recorded SR 97 from AM.PM's own /pplp/85201/... taxonomy. That taxonomy publishes no bathroom node, so a taxonomy-only reading would have returned NO BATHROOM FOUND and silently dropped 15 real AM.PM bathroom products. Because ?brndid=ampm URLs are the site's own verified category listing URLs carrying their own exact rendered totals, they are recorded here, and the taxonomy-side absence is documented above so the two readings are reconcilable. The recorded URLs do not collide with any /pplp/85201/... URL the Furniture pass took. QTY: every qty is the rendered listing header, the <span id="ProductCount"> immediately after the h1, cross-checked on every row against the grid's own data-totalproduct attribute - the two agreed on every node. CHILDREN-SUM-TO-PARENT: Organisation de la salle de bain AM.PM 10 = Panier a linge AM.PM 10, its only child, exact. Miroir AM.PM 64 splits into Miroir mural + Miroir de salle de bain (4). SUBSET SANITY CHECK: on every node where the filter applied, the AM.PM count is strictly and dramatically smaller than the unfiltered count (1 < 1673, 4 < 296, 10 < 2180, 64 < 1790, 6 < 2878), the expected brand-subset relation. CROSS-REPRESENTATION CHECK: AM.PM's own Linge de bain node (cat-85264, 6) and the main-tree cat-84135?brndid=ampm (6) return the identical count, independent evidence that the brand filter reproduces the AM.PM catalogue rather than some other slice. DRIFT CHECK: all recorded and reviewed leaves were re-fetched cache-cold in a second pass and every ProductCount and data-totalproduct came back identical (75495 1, 385864 10, 75497 10, 75496 4, 75456 64, 84135 6, 85264 6, 285674 66). COUNTS DISCRIMINATE across the AM.PM tree from 1 to 1600. EXCLUDED / ROUTED: see `review` - Linge de bain (6) routed to Textile; AM.PM's own decorative Miroir node (66) and the main-tree Miroir parent (64) not recorded (rules 21, 24); the three empty Meuble de salle de bain children, the three empty Organisation siblings and the entire empty Bricolage sanitaryware branch logged as no-AM.PM-subset; AM.PM > Luminaire (182) inspected per rule 19 and found to contain no bathroom-lighting node, so nothing was routed to Lighting. 'Panier a linge' IS recorded as Bathroom because La Redoute files it under 'Organisation de la salle de bain' (rules 12, 13 keep bathroom baskets in Bathroom). DEDUP: dedup.already_extracted() was run on all eight candidate and review URLs; none is in the exclusion index. The 26 AM.PM URLs Furniture.xlsx holds are all /pplp/85201/... furniture nodes and none overlaps anything here.
